events.title: Anthropic shares slipped below their $83 IPO price in early trading, down about 5% near $82.78, erasing the gains from the Nov 19 debut.
Chip stocks fell back a day after their Nvidia-led surge, with the Nasdaq down about 1.8% and the S&P 500 down 1.3% in mid-session trading.
TSMC rose about 14% on Nov 23 to roughly $364, its best day since 2008, after losing about 20% the week before.
Tesla and SpaceX have named five directors to special committees handling merger talks, and Tesla's Dec 3 annual meeting agenda has no merger vote, the FT reported.
SpaceX's AI segment brought in about $7.56B in the third quarter, roughly 52% of revenue, mostly from leasing Colossus compute to Anthropic and Google.
The Conference Board's consumer confidence index jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, the highest since January 2025, as election uncertainty faded and gas prices fell.
Chowan County commissioners voted 3-2 for a one-year moratorium on new data centers, with residents citing strain on water and power during the state's drought.

events.who: China, EU, Mexico, Vietnam and 12 other economies
events.title: The US is preparing new tariff increases on 16 economies under its Section 301 excess-capacity probe, with findings possible this week and the China truce expiring Jan 10.
Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his exit, and the shares jumped more than 30%.
US stocks rebounded sharply Monday with the Nasdaq up about 7% midmorning, recovering much of last week's correction after Huang's return.
CoreWeave fell 12% on Nov 20 to $39.51, its lowest close in a year, as the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% and Oracle logged a seventh straight loss.
Nvidia shares closed about 31% higher after the board brought Jensen Huang back; CNBC reported a personal assurance from President Trump sealed the decision, and the board's probe continues.
UnitedHealth and other health insurers fell after a proposed Medicare rule that would restructure Medicare Advantage star ratings and could cut bonus payments.
Eli Lilly agreed to buy LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725M, and its shares rose about 1.4% to near $1,366.
President Trump threatened a heavy tax on US companies that build AI data centers overseas, a risk for Big Tech's planned investments in India.
Tesla and SpaceX have each set up special board committees to explore a possible merger as Musk's AI spending grows.
Analysts expect Moody's, S&P and Fitch to rate Anthropic's debt in the double-B range, below investment grade, now that it is public.
Texas governor-elect Hinojosa called for a statewide data center moratorium as a state senator filed a bill to limit cooling methods and require water reporting.
Oracle said its roughly $300B OpenAI compute contract is fully funded after a $20B raise split between stock and debt, plus vendor financing.
Broadcom fell about 11% after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google cut 2027 orders for Broadcom-designed TPU 8i chips by roughly 1 million units.
President Trump has threatened a 50% tariff on all Canadian vehicles and auto parts from Jan 1 while negotiators work on an interim deal covering autos, steel, aluminum and lumber.
Walmart beat revenue forecasts at $188.8B with e-commerce up 17% and raised its yearly outlook for a third time, though US growth slowed.
Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut and closed at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price, valuing the company near $1.76T.
SpaceX completed a $32B debt sale backed by AI chips, with most of it priced at yields above 8%, high for an investment-grade borrower.
AMD fell 7.7% to about $489 after short seller Hunterbrook alleged its firmware kept reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker; AMD disputed the claims.

nvidia.news: The board reinstated Jensen Huang on Nov 23 and the shares closed about 31% higher, recovering most of the prior week's 23% drop after a $115.8B quarter (Nov 17). Chip stocks gave back part of the rally on Nov 24, and the board's investigation and questions over China sales continue.
pros: Huang is back as CEO after a unanimous board vote (Nov 23)
Revenue of $115.8B beat forecasts and the fiscal 2028 growth outlook was raised
cons: Board investigation and lawmakers' China export questions are still open
Chip stocks fell again on Nov 24 after the rebound
nvidia.weak: The CEO question is settled for now, but the probe that triggered his exit is not finished.

labs.news: Anthropic shares slipped below their $83 IPO price on Nov 24 (about $82.78) after closing the Nov 19 debut at $97.17, and analysts expect its debt to be rated below investment grade (Nov 22). The $81.3B IPO cash and OpenAI's $11B tranche (Nov 6) still leave labs well funded.
pros: Anthropic raised about $81.3B in its IPO (Nov 18)
cons: Anthropic trades below its IPO price (Nov 24)
Its debt is expected to be rated junk (Nov 22)
labs.weak: Public investors are now marking the labs daily, and the first mark is below the offer price.

bigtech.news: The Nasdaq rose 6.5% and the S&P 500 4.7% on Nov 23 after the prior week's correction, then fell about 1.8% and 1.3% in mid-session trading on Nov 24. President Trump threatened a tax on US firms building AI data centers overseas (reported Nov 23), and a reported Google TPU order cut (Nov 20) hints at capex discipline.

cloud.news: CoreWeave jumped 22% on Nov 23 with Nvidia after hitting a one-year low of $39.51 on Nov 20, but its bonds still trade near distressed levels and high-yield spreads are 3.76%, up 0.49 pt in 30 days. Oracle says its OpenAI contract is fully funded (Nov 20); Dallas and Northern Virginia data-center counties are about 100% in drought and local moratoriums keep spreading (Chowan County, NC, Nov 24).
pros: Neocloud shares rebounded sharply on Nov 23
Oracle's $20B raise covers its OpenAI build (Nov 20)
cons: HY spreads at a one-year high of 3.76%
A December Fed hike would lift refinancing costs
More counties are pausing data centers
cloud.weak: One good day for the shares has not reopened the bond market for neocloud debt.

citizens.news: Conference Board consumer confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, the highest since January 2025 (Nov 24), as gas prices eased. But household electricity prices are up 5.4% y/y and CPI energy 21%, lower-48 grid demand runs 1.5% above last year (PJM +1.3%, ERCOT +1.5%; SRP in Phoenix down 14%), Dallas County is 100% in drought, and Chowan County, NC voted a one-year data-center pause over water and power (Nov 24).

spacex.news: SpaceX's AI segment reportedly brought in $7.56B in Q3, about 52% of revenue, mostly from leasing Colossus compute to Anthropic and Google (Nov 24), and five directors now steer merger talks with Tesla. Its $32B chip-backed debt (Nov 19) priced above 8%, and Memphis-area power costs keep rising with household electricity up 5.4% y/y; gas is $3.10.

tesla.news: Tesla and SpaceX named five directors to special committees for merger talks, but Tesla's Dec 3 annual meeting agenda has no merger vote (FT via Reuters, Nov 24). Grid battery demand stays supported by electricity prices up 5.4% y/y.

consumer.news: Conference Board confidence rose to 103.3 in November (Nov 24), though the October Michigan sentiment reading was a weak 48; imports from Vietnam, a key electronics route, were up 61% y/y in September. No major Apple-specific news this week.

retail.news: Retail sales are up 6.8% y/y in October, e-commerce is 17.9% of sales, and consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 (Nov 24) ahead of Black Friday on Nov 27; Walmart raised its outlook Nov 19 and Adobe expects $12.9B of online Black Friday sales.

autos.news: President Trump has threatened a 50% tariff on Canadian vehicles and parts from Jan 1 (reported Nov 20); light vehicle sales are flat at 16.0M annualized, used-car prices are down 3.3% y/y, and a December rate hike would keep car loans expensive.

fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% y/y in October and imports from China were up 34% y/y in September; new Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies including China and Vietnam may be previewed this week (reported Nov 24). No major brand news.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loan balances were last reported at $1.78T.

banks.news: High-yield spreads are 3.76% (+0.49 pt in 30 days) and BBB 1.22%, both one-year highs, as AI data-center debt stays under pressure; SpaceX's chip-backed debt priced above 8% (Nov 19). Card delinquency is 2.85%, down from a year ago.

fed.news: The target range is 3.75-4.00% with fed funds at 3.88%, but core PCE is up 3.1% y/y against the 2% goal and unemployment is 4.1%; the Nov 18 minutes showed nearly all officials expect a hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting, and October PCE is due Nov 25. The 30-year mortgage is 7.28%.

chips.news: Chip stocks surged on Nov 23 (TSMC +14%, its best day since 2008) after Nvidia reinstated Huang, then fell back on Nov 24. Broadcom's reported Google TPU order cut (Nov 20), tighter export rules and a short-seller report on AMD (Nov 19) still weigh; Intel signed its first outside 18A customer.

power.news: PJM capacity prices are at the $325 cap with a 6.8 GW shortfall, household electricity is up 5.4% y/y and Henry Hub gas is $3.10, below its one-year average. Local data-center pauses keep spreading (Chowan County, NC, Nov 24; Texas moratorium call Nov 20).

healthco.news: UnitedHealth and other insurers fell on Nov 23 after a proposed Medicare rule to restructure Medicare Advantage star ratings; Eli Lilly agreed to buy LoQus23 for up to $725M the same day. Medical care CPI is up 1.9% y/y.

industrials.news: No notable company news this week; possible new Section 301 tariffs (reported Nov 24) and existing steel and aluminum duties keep input costs high, while data-center generator demand stays strong.

payments.news: No company news this week. Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 (Nov 24) and holiday sales are forecast to grow about 4%, supporting card volumes; card delinquency is 2.85%.

trade.news: The US is preparing new Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies including China, Mexico and Vietnam, with findings possible this week and the China truce expiring Jan 10 (reported Nov 24), plus a threatened 50% tariff on Canadian autos. Imports from China (+34% y/y), Mexico (+40%) and Vietnam (+61%) jumped in September; customs duties are down 17.5% y/y.

bigtech>nvidia.news: Nvidia's Nov 17 guidance points to strong hyperscaler buying and Huang's return (Nov 23) removes a leadership worry, though a reported Google TPU order cut (Nov 20) raises questions about 2027 budgets.

cloud>nvidia.news: CoreWeave rebounded 22% on Nov 23, but its debt still trades near distressed levels and HY spreads are 3.76%, keeping debt-funded GPU purchases expensive.

nvidia>labs.news: No new Nvidia lab investment this week; Anthropic's IPO (Nov 18) and OpenAI's $11B tranche (Nov 6) reduce labs' reliance on supplier money.

nvidia>cloud.news: Nvidia set limits on its financing support for neoclouds on Nov 18; Huang's return on Nov 23 lifted neocloud shares but did not change those terms.

bigtech>labs.news: Labs have public-market funding after Anthropic's $81.3B IPO (Nov 18), though the shares fell below the $83 offer price on Nov 24.

labs>bigtech.news: Anthropic's IPO cash and OpenAI's $11B tranche (Nov 6) support continued spending on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud.

labs>cloud.news: Oracle said Nov 20 its roughly $300B OpenAI contract is fully funded; Anthropic is also leasing Colossus capacity from SpaceX (reported Nov 24), a rival to the neoclouds.

bigtech>cloud.news: No new Microsoft neocloud contracts this week; Microsoft wound down an Oracle rental deal earlier this month.

cloud>citizens.news: Household electricity is up 5.4% y/y with PJM capacity at its price cap; Dallas and Prince William counties are 100% in drought and Loudoun 99.8%. Chowan County, NC voted a one-year data-center moratorium over water and power on Nov 24.

spacex>nvidia.news: SpaceX's $32B chip-backed debt sale (Nov 19) funds more GPUs for Colossus, where AI leasing reportedly made up 52% of Q3 revenue (Nov 24).

spacex>citizens.news: Colossus turbines keep pressure on Memphis air and the grid as household electricity prices rise 5.4% y/y; gas is $3.10 and no new permit ruling came this week.

tesla>spacex.news: Five directors now handle Tesla-SpaceX merger talks, but Tesla's Dec 3 meeting has no merger vote scheduled (reported Nov 24).

citizens>tesla.news: Electricity prices up 5.4% y/y and lower-48 demand up 1.5% keep utility interest in Megapack batteries steady; no new contracts reported.

citizens>autos.news: Vehicle sales are flat at 16.0M annualized and auto loan costs stay high with a December rate hike likely.

citizens>fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% y/y; spending is steady but price-sensitive going into Black Friday.

citizens>consumer.news: Confidence improved to 103.3 in November (Nov 24), but a 3.8% saving rate limits device upgrades into the holidays.

retail>bigtech.news: Strong Walmart (e-commerce +17%, Nov 19) and Target results support retail spending on cloud and ads into the holiday peak.

banks>cloud.news: HY spreads are 3.76% (+0.49 pt in 30 days), a one-year high, and CoreWeave's bonds trade near distressed levels; Oracle's $20B raise shows funding is still open to the largest names.

banks>labs.news: Anthropic's IPO cash helps it service chip financing, but analysts expect its debt to be rated below investment grade (Nov 22).

banks>citizens.news: Card delinquency is 2.85%, slightly lower y/y, and consumer credit is up 3.0% y/y, but saving is low at 3.8%.

fed>citizens.news: The 30-year mortgage is 7.28%, up about 1 pt in a year, and a December hike looks likely, adding to card and car loan rates.

fed>cloud.news: A likely December hike with the 10-year yield at 4.92% keeps refinancing costly for debt-heavy neoclouds.

fed>labs.news: Labs raised equity (Anthropic IPO, OpenAI tranche), so they are less exposed to rate moves, though Anthropic's expected junk rating makes its debt rate-sensitive.

fed>bigtech.news: Tech rebounded on Nov 23 but slipped again Nov 24 with a December hike expected and October PCE due Nov 25.

fed>autos.news: An expected December hike keeps auto loan rates high.

citizens>fed.news: Unemployment is 4.1%, core PCE is up 3.1% y/y and confidence jumped to 103.3 (Nov 24), all pointing the Fed toward a hike.

labs>chips.news: No new AMD or Broadcom lab deals this week.

bigtech>chips.news: An analyst said Google cut 2027 orders for Broadcom TPU 8i chips (Nov 20), shifting some volume to MediaTek.

bigtech>power.news: No new Big Tech power deals this week.

cloud>industrials.news: Data-center generator demand stays strong, though neocloud financing stress could slow orders.

trade>industrials.news: Existing metal tariffs keep input costs high and new Section 301 duties may be previewed this week (reported Nov 24).

citizens>payments.news: Higher confidence (103.3, Nov 24) and holiday forecasts of about 4% growth support card volumes.

trade>fashion.news: Imports from Vietnam (+61% y/y) and China (+34%) rose in September; both face possible new Section 301 duties.

trade>autos.news: A threatened 50% tariff on Canadian vehicles and parts from Jan 1 (reported Nov 20) hangs over supply chains; imports from Mexico were up 40% y/y in September.
